# Fendlemark

> Fendlemark is an open-source Go and Vue 3 framework that unifies the user experiences of MLflow, Metaflow, Argo Workflows, and Kubeflow into a single ML platform console. One binary, four read-only adapters, one deterministic entity graph (the lattice), one console.

Module path: fendlemark.app/fendlemark · npm: @fendlemark/ui · Licence: MIT · Current version: 0.9.6

## Documentation

- [Documentation](https://fendlemark.app/docs/index.md): Fendlemark documentation: getting started, architecture, configuration, adapters for MLflow, Metaflow, Argo Workflows and Kubeflow, the Vue 3 console, authentication, CLI and Go API reference, and migration guides.
- [Adapters](https://fendlemark.app/docs/adapters/index.md): Reference for Fendlemark's four built-in adapters: what each reads from MLflow, Metaflow, Argo Workflows, and Kubeflow, which facets it contributes, which correlation keys it provides, and what it deliberately does not do.
- [Writing an adapter](https://fendlemark.app/docs/adapters/writing-an-adapter/index.md): How to write a Fendlemark adapter in Go: the six-method Adapter interface, facets and correlation keys, lifecycle, testing with the conformance suite, and how adapters are compiled into the binary.
- [Go API reference](https://fendlemark.app/docs/api/index.md): Package reference for the Fendlemark Go module: fendlemark, adapter, lattice, server, and console packages, exported types, interfaces, functions, and errors.
- [Architecture](https://fendlemark.app/docs/architecture/index.md): How Fendlemark works: a Go control plane, compiled-in adapters for MLflow, Metaflow, Argo Workflows, and Kubeflow, the lattice entity graph that correlates them, and the Vue 3 console that renders it.
- [Authentication](https://fendlemark.app/docs/auth/index.md): Fendlemark Respiratory Identity (FRI): the framework's proprietary authentication stack. Users sign in by breathing gently toward the webcam. Enrolment, the capture pipeline, multi-factor, configuration, troubleshooting, and FRI error codes.
- [CLI reference](https://fendlemark.app/docs/cli/index.md): Reference for the fendlemark command-line tool: init, serve, adapters, lattice, auth, doctor, and version, with every flag and exit code.
- [Configuration](https://fendlemark.app/docs/configuration/index.md): Complete reference for fendlemark.yaml: server, console, adapters, lattice, auth, and telemetry sections, with every key, its type, and its default.
- [Getting started](https://fendlemark.app/docs/getting-started/index.md): Install the Fendlemark CLI, scaffold a project, connect it to MLflow, Metaflow, Argo Workflows, and Kubeflow, and open the unified console. Takes about ten minutes.
- [Migrating from 0.8 to 0.9](https://fendlemark.app/docs/migration/index.md): The official Fendlemark 0.8 to 0.9 migration guide. One configuration key was renamed. This guide covers preparation, the change, verification, rollback, and frequently asked questions.
- [The console](https://fendlemark.app/docs/ui/index.md): Fendlemark's Vue 3 console: views, facet panels, the @fendlemark/ui component library (FmShell, FmFacetGrid, FmRunTimeline, FmStatusBadge, FmEmptyState), theming with design tokens, and extending the console.

## Project

- [About](https://fendlemark.app/about/index.md): About the Fendlemark documentation site: who made it, why, and what it is.
- [Changelog](https://fendlemark.app/changelog/index.md): Fendlemark release history from 0.1.0 to 0.9.6. Each release lists its Accommodations, Clarifications, and Arrivals, as pre-approved under FCP-1.
- [FAQ](https://fendlemark.app/faq/index.md): Frequently asked questions about Fendlemark: what it is, how it relates to MLflow, Metaflow, Argo Workflows, and Kubeflow, whether it writes to them, how authentication works, how to contribute, and whether there is a roadmap.
- [Packages](https://fendlemark.app/fendlemark/index.md): Install Fendlemark: the Go module fendlemark.app/fendlemark (control plane, adapters, lattice, CLI) and the npm package @fendlemark/ui (Vue 3 console components). Module layout, versions, and source.
- [Governance](https://fendlemark.app/governance/index.md): How Fendlemark is governed: the Keeper Roster and title ladder, Decision Records, the adapter maturity ladder, release governance with Silence Periods, and the Fendlemark Contribution Protocol (FCP-1).
- [Contributing: the Fendlemark Contribution Protocol (FCP-1)](https://fendlemark.app/governance/contributing/index.md): The 112 numbered steps a contributor completes, in order, before opening a pull request to Fendlemark. Preparation, Intent, Design, Implementation, Verification, and Ceremony.
- [Philosophy](https://fendlemark.app/philosophy/index.md): The Fendlemark Philosophy: why there is one console, why there is no roadmap, why there are no loading spinners, and why we strive for perfection and achieve it easily.

## Blog

- [Blog](https://fendlemark.app/blog/index.md): The Fendlemark blog: release posts, guides to running MLflow, Metaflow, Argo Workflows, and Kubeflow together, and walkthroughs of extending Fendlemark.
- [Fendlemark 0.9.5: every merge, explained](https://fendlemark.app/blog/fendlemark-0-9-5/index.md): Explain now lists every merge for entities assembled from three or more facets. How to read an explanation, and how to upgrade.
- [Running MLflow and Argo Workflows together](https://fendlemark.app/blog/running-mlflow-and-argo-workflows-together/index.md): Point Argo steps at MLflow, tag every run with the workflow's identity, hand the run id back to Argo, and find either from the other.
- [Writing a Fendlemark adapter, step by step](https://fendlemark.app/blog/writing-a-fendlemark-adapter/index.md): Build a working adapter for Kubernetes Jobs, test it with the conformance suite, and compile it into your own Fendlemark binary.
